title: H-G full: does the shipped gstack /investigate skill help Opus on bug-fix tasks?
question: With the full shipped skill in place of the stripped copy of the 2026-11-10 H-G run, does the told arm pass more often than the none arm on the same two fixtures?

redactions: home-relative path of the gstack state folder replaced by <home>/.gstack
home-relative path of the Claude config file replaced by <home>/.claude.json
home-relative path of the gstack state folder replaced by <home>/.gstack

verdict.label: hypothesis-supported
verdict.text: DECISION: H-G SUPPORTED (not contradicted at n=8; ceiling in fx3). This is absence of a detected benefit, not evidence of zero effect.

notes: n = 8 per arm per fixture, Opus, 30 turns. 31 usable trials of 32. The trial fx3-told-8 is missing: the usage limit ended the run cap.

The told-full arm is a different treatment from the told arm of 2026-11-10-hg-gstack-investigate, which used a stripped copy. The two are separate groups. The none arm is a same-day rerun of that run's none arm and shares its group.
Descriptive comparison from the analyzer: told-full 9/15 against stripped told 8/16 pooled. Fresh none 14/16 against earlier none 13/16.
The told arm costs about 1.9 times the none arm per trial (0.516 against 0.275 USD).
